newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end financial year at record high.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end financial year at record high.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.915 +0.040 Gold NY 334.55 Lon fix 336.55
AUD US$0.7453 (Fri cl$0.7485) CRB Index cl 239.33 -0.07
*Stocks at new highs on U.S. gains, financial year end, and hopes of domestic ratE cut. BHP strong. Volume 546.6 million, value A$930.5 million, 1,306 stocks traded, 344 steady, 522 up, 440 down.

Australian shares rose to a record closing high on Monday following U.S. gains on Friday and as some investors speculated that the Reserve Bank would announce another rate cut after its meeting on Tuesday.
Trading became active and gains stronger towards the end as fund managers moved to close books for the financial year-end.
At 4.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 23.5 points higher at a record close at 2,725.9. Total turnover amounted to a fairly high A$930 million.
June share price index futures were 27 points up at 2,726, a marginal premium to the underlying index.

"There was a lot of book-squaring going on at the end, and some will take a new look at the books in the morning," one Sydney-based dealer said. He added that although Tuesday would be largely governed by movements on Wall Street, sentiment was firm with healthy buying from overseas.
Blue chip stock Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd rose 33.3 cents to A$19.483 after Friday's full-year report and on positive outlook comments from managing director John Prescott.
BHP's net profit slumped due to one-off net abnormal losses, but pre-abnormal earnings were in line with expectations and dealers said the company now looks set to improve profits.

"On the back of Wall Street and BHP going up, the market really hasn't done anything suprising," one dealer said. "Steady as she goes, it will probably rise a bit further this week if the Reserve Bank and Fed hold rates," he added.
The U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committe meets Tuesday and Wednesday, and the market expects rates to be held steady.

Banking lost some of its early gains, but the sector index ended 1.2 percent higher on speculation of an imminent domestic rate cut. National Australia Bank rose 17 cents to A$18.97, while Westpac Banking climbed 17 to A$7.07 and Commonwealth Bank ended 26 cents up at an even A$16.
The gold sector was hurt by a slump in gold prices to a four year low of U$334.00 an ounce over the weekend, but shares started to recover in late trade.
The sector index fell 0.5 percent with Normandy Mining and Lihir Gold both down two cents to A$1.49 and A$2.21 respectively. Western Mining lost 5 cents to A$8.35

Coca-Cola Amatil closed 52 cents up at A$17.20 ahead of Tuesday's extraordinary general meeting at which shareholders are due to vote on a A$3.4 billion share swap with the Philippines' San Miguel Corp.
"I didn't expect them to break 17 dollars even with book-squaring going on. It's a mystery to me," said one dealer.
Brambles Industries was also among the winners, rising 58 cents to A$25.99. "There was some buying interest from overseas," one dealer noted.
ICI Australia Ltd shares ended 16 cents up at A$13.05 after Wesfarmers Ltd said it had held unsuccessful discussions with Imperial Chemical Industries Plc to bid for the Australian subsidiary.
Shares in transport and health care group Mayne Nickless fell eight cents to A$7.72.

Some dealers said the decline could be linked to Mayne's stake in Optus Communications. Cable and Wireless Plc had not yet approached the Australian government about lifting its stake in Optus, a government spokesman said earlier on Monday.
BellSouth has said it would like to sell its 24.5 percent stake in Optus well before the float, due sometime next year.

Auto parts company Hawker Richardson rose 11 cents to A$1.86, spot on a new take-over offer from Austrim. A A$1.60 per share bid was rejected last week, but Hawker has recommended acceptance of the new bid.
In other markets, Australian bonds firmed in afternoon trade on optimism ahead of the Reserve Bank meeting on Tuesday. The 10-year T-bond was at 92.915 by 4.15 p.m. (0415 GMT).
At the same time, the Australian dollar suffered its lowest close for 17 months at US$0.7455.
